uncited: It differs from [Water Surface Rendering](5636-water-surface-rendering.md) and [Stream Surface Rendering](7716-stream-surface-rendering.md) by treating the geometry as opaque or skeletal primitives rather than fluid or flow-based surfaces.
Time and memory complexity are linear with respect to the number of faces and vertices.
Solid mode is generally faster than wireframe mode as it involves fewer draw calls (one per face vs. three per face for edges).
Wireframe mode provides better visibility of internal structure but may suffer from aliasing on thin edges.
Solid mode is suitable for opaque objects, while wireframe is useful for debugging or transparent overlays.
Originated in early computer graphics for visualizing 3D models.
